CAUSAL CLOSURE AND PHYSICAL ADMISSION WITH RETAINED QUANTUM APPARATUS
Astra P2, Phase 8. Root construction and synthesis. 1 November 2026.

Scope
=====
This is a finite-operation and finite-lifetime theorem in explicitly stated
open-system models. It supplies a physical route from continuous bosonic noise
and calibration errors to a joint fault expansion consumed by an actual noisy
receiver. It is not an acquired hardware threshold or a claim of priority for
geometric gates, temporal-mode filtering, subsystem correction, bosonic
truncation, or non-Markovian fault tolerance. The decisive microscopic
compatibility obstruction is retained, not hidden in an ideal control.

The inherited Phase7 two-mode half-turn, exact loss-overlap operator, repeated
Bacon-Shor recovery, protected classical controller and consumed CNOT remain
unchanged in the cumulative packet. The replacement below is a different
effective apparatus. Its finite direct readout port is not an elimination of
the inherited finite buffer at an unjustified rate.

1. What must be removed from an old apparatus?
=============================================
Let D be the useful data, M the apparatus that survives an operation, R an
arbitrary reference, and F the fresh input field. M can be nonGaussian, warm,
and entangled with D and R. F is independent of DMR. Returning field modes are
part of M, not fresh F. The delivered record is C; analog records that are
actually retained and later used must also be included.

The weakest useful exact interface is record-inclusive absence of influence:

 Tr_M' Lambda_DC M' = I_DC o Tr_M                         (1)

for one fixed quantum-classical instrument I and EVERY input DMR. This is an
identity of complete maps, not a statement only on product inputs. Composing
such instruments with arbitrary causal data/record operations preserves (1)
over every unnormalized history. Induct on the operations, keeping R and all
previous records. Conditional probabilities may be arbitrarily large on a
rare normalized branch; the complete-history identity does not require a
conditional energy estimate.

Outcome-summed absence of influence is weaker than (1). A later measurement of
an old apparatus correlated with D can condition D even if the averaged D map
was independent of M. Thus neither a data marginal nor an average cavity
occupation is the desired instrument contract.

# Final scientific boundary and capability audit

Audited: `phase8/root/CAUSAL_CLOSURE_AND_JOINT_ADMISSION.txt`.

## Decision

The general passive-scattering result is a useful physical interface theorem. It can be sharpened to a necessary-and-sufficient statement for an **unmeasured controlled-displacement product channel** under finite homogeneous thermal/vacuum input, after removing data-independent displacements. It cannot be advertised as a universally necessary two-closure boundary for an arbitrary terminal measurement instrument. A terminal measurement may intentionally erase the coherence that carries incoming-memory dependence; a record-inclusive no-influence instrument also need not have a product retained channel.

The exact full-instrument boundary is the record-inclusive complete-map identity in root Eq. (1). The two closures are a constructive criterion for the stronger gate-channel interface, and in the stated homogeneous Gaussian setting they are generically necessary for that stronger interface.

The justified scientific advance is physical admission and interface construction for a retained unbounded bosonic apparatus, joined to a real noisy receiver. No demonstrated information-processing capability exceeds the finite dirty-qubit comparator or ordinary fault-tolerant encoded circuits. The bosonic dynamics and physical-admission result remain nontrivial even though the resulting parity and consumed CNOT capabilities are conventional.

\[

\[
 \delta d_z=d_z-d_{z_0}.
\]
